title: Single-Cell Transcriptional Analysis Reveals the Mechanism of AZD6738 in HCC Immunotherapy via EZH2 Targeting.
authors: Li, Ren-Peng; Wu, Guo-Zhi; Fang, Xi-Dong; Yang, Wen-Wen; Zhang, Hui-Yun; Yue, Han-Xun; Zheng, Ya; Wang, Yu-Ping; Zhou, Yong-Ning
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过转录组和单细胞分析探讨AZD6738靶向EZH2在肝癌免疫治疗中的作用，虽含分子对接但核心是药物机制与免疫表型，非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，与本课题关联弱。
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aims to identify specific molecular targets sensitive to AZD6738 through the integration of network pharmacology and transcriptomic methods, and to assess their potential role in the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Additionally, we explore the specific effects of AZD6738 on the tumor microenvironment and its ability to regulate immune responses. METHODS: We employed a combination of network pharmacology and transcriptomic analysis to identify specific molecules associated with HCC, including EZH2, CCNB1, PRKDC, CTSL, PSEN1, SLC6A3, and FKBP1A. Using these molecules and clinical features, we constructed a robust prognostic model for HCC. We further used single-cell transcriptomic technology to screen for core targets and performed spatial transcriptomic analysis to determine their spatial distribution. To validate the efficacy of AZD6738 in vivo, we established a subcutaneous tumor model, with the experimental group receiving oral administration of AZD6738 (75 mg/kg). Finally, we assessed the changes in the immune cell expression profile in tumor tissues post-AZD6738 treatment using flow cytometry. RESULTS: Our study indicates that the high expression of genes such as EZH2, CCNB1, PRKDC, and PSEN1 is associated with poor prognosis in HCC patients. Molecular docking and RT-PCR validation demonstrated that AZD6738 exhibits high affinity for these targets and significantly reduces the mRNA levels of EZH2, PRKDC, and CCNB1 in HCC cell lines, with EZH2 showing the most pronounced decrease. Animal experiments revealed that AZD6738 can enhance the immune microenvironment in liver cancer; specifically, AZD6738 not only promotes the proliferation of CD8+ T cells but also enhances their differentiation into effector memory T cells, indicating that the drug can potentiate anti-tumor immune responses. CONCLUSION: This study reveals that AZD6738 demonstrates significant therapeutic efficacy by targeting the key molecule EZH2, thereby modulating the tumor microenvironment and enhancing anti-tumor immunity.
abstract_zh: 目的：本研究旨在通过整合网络药理学与转录组学方法，识别对AZD6738敏感的特定分子靶点，并评估其在肝细胞癌（HCC）治疗中的潜在作用。此外，我们探讨AZD6738对肿瘤微环境的具体影响及其调节免疫反应的能力。方法：我们采用网络药理学与转录组学分析相结合的方法，识别与HCC相关的特定分子，包括EZH2、CCNB1、PRKDC、CTSL、PSEN1、SLC6A3和FKBP1A。利用这些分子及临床特征，我们构建了一个稳健的HCC预后模型。我们进一步使用单细胞转录组学技术筛选核心靶点，并进行空间转录组学分析以确定其空间分布。为验证AZD6738在体内的疗效，我们建立了皮下肿瘤模型，实验组口服给予AZD6738（75 mg/kg）。最后，我们通过流式细胞术评估了AZD6738治疗后肿瘤组织中免疫细胞表达谱的变化。结果：我们的研究表明，EZH2、CCNB1、PRKDC和PSEN1等基因的高表达与HCC患者的不良预后相关。分子对接和RT-PCR验证表明，AZD6738对这些靶点具有高亲和力，并显著降低HCC细胞系中EZH2、PRKDC和CCNB1的mRNA水平，其中EZH2的下降最为显著。动物实验显示，AZD6738能增强肝癌中的免疫微环境；具体而言，AZD6738不仅促进CD8+ T细胞的增殖，还增强其分化为效应记忆T细胞，表明该药物能增强抗肿瘤免疫反应。结论：本研究揭示AZD6738通过靶向关键分子EZH2，调节肿瘤微环境并增强抗肿瘤免疫，展现出显著的治疗效果。
